source.title: BLIA: Detect model memorization in binary classification model through passive Label Inference attack
source.authors: Mohammad Wahiduzzaman Khan; Sheng Chen; Ilya Mironov; Lei-Zhen Zhang; Rabib Noor

record.file_problem: Full paper text and appendix are present; some table columns are flattened, but the reported values can be assigned from their headings and accompanying text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures inference of deliberately flipped training labels as evidence of memorization, using attack accuracy rather than directly testing the listed versions’ natural-label held-out generalization claims.
record.gate_note: The study flips labels for 2% of training examples with 50% probability, then reports attack accuracy and training accuracy. It does not report held-out accuracy on natural labels or test error, so these results do not test whether memorization of random labels coexists with natural-label generalization. Attack-method comparisons and most intermediate privacy-budget results are not included in the rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures label-inference attack accuracy on randomized training canaries, not any version's generalization outcome. It reports neither held-out performance establishing V1's coexistence claim nor the comparisons required by V2–V8. Its discussion of memorization and generalization does not constitute a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they interpret passive inference of randomized canary labels as evidence of memorization persisting under randomized-response Label-DP. However, their assertion of consistently above-chance success overstates the tables, which contain below-chance results and many near-chance values without uncertainty estimates. They do not demonstrate any held-out generalization effect.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses passive black-box label-inference accuracy on a 2% subset of deliberately flipped training labels and randomized-response Label-DP. It does not reproduce the original sources’ natural-label test-error, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, width, sharpness, or example-removal measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, attack type, and privacy budget change the reported attack accuracies; the delta-margin attack is generally more successful than the threshold attack, with exceptions in reported values.

fits_no_version.finding: Attack accuracy on randomized training canaries varies by dataset, attack, and privacy budget. At epsilon = 0.3, delta-margin accuracy is 89.20% on IMDB, 82.75% on FashionMNIST, and 76.00% on CIFAR-100, but 48.90% on CIFAR-10. Several other results remain near 50%. These measure label leakage rather than held-out generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Outputs and per-sample losses of binary classifiers can reveal randomized training-canary labels, with attack success depending on the dataset, attack, and randomized-response privacy budget.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Only binary classification is studied, canaries are limited to 2% of training data, and no natural-label held-out accuracy or test error is reported. Several attack accuracies are near the 50% baseline. The paper's text says labels in the canary subset are flipped with 50% probability, while its tables report attack accuracies without uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Training-accuracy values are reported in Tables 2–8 but omitted because they do not measure held-out generalization or label-inference success. Intermediate privacy-budget rows (ϵ = ∞, 4, 2, 1, 0.8, 0.5) are omitted to stay within the row limit and retain the no-Label-DP results plus the ϵ = 0.3 endpoints. The paper's discussion also gives some approximate repeated values; table values are used where available.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy using the same architecture and recipe, and chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification test error and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes, configurations, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions. The attack accuracies remain useful descriptive results under fits_no_version. The 2% figure denotes the selected canary subset, within which labels are independently flipped with 50% probability; it does not mean 2% of all labels necessarily change. Cross-dataset architecture differences do not supply a controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out accuracy on natural labels, no random-label training accuracy, and no comparison of natural-label and random-label generalization.
No network-width sweep or test-error measurements.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison on image test error.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal and retraining of memorized examples.
